[2026-08-26T22:11:36.845Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5870b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":68801,\"title\":\"Remove the Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults OTLP export workaround after OpenTelemetry supports async export\",\"body\":\"### Description\\n\\nThe Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults template currently uses `BackgroundExportHandler` to work around synchronous OTLP export on single-threaded WebAssembly.\\n\\nOpenTelemetry\\u0026#39;s OTLP exporter calls:\\n\\n```csharp\\nHttpClient.SendAsync(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult()\\n```\\n\\nThis can stall when the HTTP pipeline performs asynchronous work. The template handler avoids that stall by capturing the request, immediately returning a synthetic successful response, and sending the real request asynchronously through a Polly resilience pipeline.\\n\\nOpenTelemetry added task-based batch and metric workers for single-threaded WebAssembly in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#6379, but the worker still invokes the synchronous exporter contract. The remaining limitation is tracked by open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708.\\n\\nOnce that issue is resolved and the fix is available in a stable OpenTelemetry release, remove the template workaround and use the standard OTLP exporter implementation.\\n\\n### Proposed changes\\n\\n- Update the Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults OpenTelemetry dependencies to a stable version containing the fix for open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708.\\n- Delete `BackgroundExportHandler.cs`.\\n- Remove the custom `IPostConfigureOptions` configuration that supplies `BackgroundExportHandler`.\\n- Remove the custom `ResiliencePipelineBuilder` configuration.\\n- Remove the `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` dependency if it is no longer otherwise needed.\\n- Configure logs, traces, and metrics using the standard `AddOtlpExporter` APIs.\\n- Allow OTLP exporters to use the normal HTTP client integration without bypassing globally configured asynchronous handlers such as service discovery.\\n\\n### Validation\\n\\nAdd or update browser integration coverage to verify that, in single-threaded Blazor WebAssembly:\\n\\n- Logs, traces, and metrics are exported successfully over OTLP/HTTP.\\n- Export works when `IHttpClientFactory` includes an asynchronous delegating handler, including the globally configured service-discovery handler used by the template.\\n- Export requests are not reported as successful before the HTTP operation completes.\\n- Export failures are surfaced through normal OpenTelemetry diagnostics.\\n- Retry, timeout, flush, and shutdown behavior use OpenTelemetry\\u0026#39;s standard semantics without fire-and-forget requests.\\n- No provider must be manually resolved to initialize OpenTelemetry; normal `IHostedService` startup remains sufficient.\\n\\n### Dependencies\\n\\nBlocked by:\\n\\n- open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708\\n\\nRelated:\\n\\n- #64574\\n- #64890\\n- #67259\\n- #67267\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68801\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-26T11:52:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T11:56:38Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Disposing an `IJSObjectReference` after the WebView had gone threw `JSDisconnectedException`, which showed up as hangs on teardown and alarming errors in the debug output. Navigation and disposal now mark the JS runtime disconnected before components are disposed, and that exception is caught and discarded.\\n\\nThis validates that a Hybrid app tears down cleanly.\\n\\n## Minimum build\\n\\n.NET 11 Preview 7 or later.\\n\\n## Configurations to cover\\n\\n* Blazor Web App\\n  * [ ] Static SSR\\n  * [ ] Interactive Server\\n  * [ ] Interactive WebAssembly\\n  * [ ] Interactive Auto\\n* [ ] Standalone WebAssembly\\n* [x] Hybrid (MAUI)\\n\\n## Also exercise\\n\\n* [ ] Published output\\n* [ ] An existing .NET 10 app upgraded to .NET 11\\n* [ ] Trimming or ahead-of-time compilation\\n* [ ] More than one server instance, or a proxy in front\\n* [ ] Hot Reload\\n* [ ] An IDE as well as the command line\\n* [ ] Container\\n\\n## Setup\\n\\nYou need the workloads for building a native app for at least one platform, and a device or emulator. Covering more than one platform is worthwhile, since the embedded browser differs between them.\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nA native app hosting Blazor, with pages that are busy in ways that make teardown awkward. Include a page that keeps a JavaScript module loaded and calls into it repeatedly, one that starts a slow JavaScript call and does not wait for it, one with a timer that keeps firing, and one that has registered .NET methods for JavaScript to call back into. Give the components proper cleanup so you can tell whether it runs. [2026-08-26T22:11:38.994Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 10652b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":66731,\"title\":\"Expose some internal Blazor APIs to allow customization for form and querystring deserialization\",\"body\":\"## Background and Motivation\\n\\nOver the last couple of months I\\u0026#39;ve logged a couple of bugs with the form / query binding in Blazor:\\n* #66607\\n* #65010\\n* #65002\\n\\nAnd now I\\u0026#39;m having another issue I\\u0026#39;m struggling with, and that\\u0026#39;s the fact that `ParsableConverter` calls `TryParse` with `reader.Culture`, and when `FormDataReader` is instantiated it\\u0026#39;s hard coded to use `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` as the culture. This is a problem for me because my website is for New Zealand and Australia and so all the date inputs format, so `InvariantCulture` will incorrectly deserialize the `DateTime` values.\\n\\nIn MVC there\\u0026#39;s similar issues, but I can create a custom implementation of `IModelBinderProvider` so I can fix it, but the relevant types here are all internal, like `FormDataConverter`, `FormDataConverter` , `ISingleValueConverter` and `FormDataMapperOptions`.  If they where public I could create my own implementation and configure `FormDataMapperOptions` to add them.\\n\\nAnother approach I tried was to create my own implementation of `SupplyParameterFromFormAttribute`. From there there\\u0026#39;s lots of approaches I could take, possibly something crazy like wrapping some calls to `IModelBinderFactory` so my MVC and Blazor code could share serialization behavior, but that\\u0026#39;s not possible either because `ICascadingValueSupplier` is also internal.\\n\\n## Proposed API\\n\\nSo I\\u0026#39;d like to propose making `ICascadingValueSupplier` public, and either making `FormDataConverter` and `ISingleValueConverter` public, or creating a new interface to implement so `FormDataReader` doesn\\u0026#39;t need to be exposed publicly also.\\n\\n## Usage Examples\\n\\n### Custom FormDataConverter\\n\\n```csharp\\nvar builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);\\n\\nbuilder.Services.Configure(options =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    options.Converters[typeof(DateTime)] = new CustomDateTimeConverter();\\n});\\n\\ninternal class CustomDateTimeConverter : FormDataConverter, ISingleValueConverter\\n{\\n    private static CultureInfo HTTP QUERY is fully supported (see #63276, #65489, #65714).\\n\\nThere was a similar discussion around that for HttpClient\\u0026#39;s instrumentation, and they decided to not implement it: Try to authentication/logout endpoint.\\n\\n**Additional context**\\n\\n- DOTNET 10\\n- Template: https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/tree/main/10.0/BlazorWebAppOidcBffAuto\\n\\nIs InteractiveWebAssembly not supported with the sample codes, or there any different changes we need to do?\\n\\n(cc: @guardrex https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/issues/642)\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/65368\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Schoof-T\",\"id\":2319986,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Schoof-T\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2319986?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-auth\",\"Needs: Attention :wave:\",\"Needs: Repro\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-02-09T12:00:32Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-19T07:44:43Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-26T22:11:47.510Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5927b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":51598,\"title\":\"[Blazor] Enable Blazor apps running inside of ASP.NET Core to be Native AoT compiled\",\"body\":\"There are several issues around this topic, and none are very explicit.\\n\\nThis issue will track the work we need to do to make this happen.\\n\\nAoT has become an important tech across the industry, with emphasis on cloud scenarios, performance and \\u0026#34;leanness\\u0026#34;. As such, it\\u0026#39;s interesting for Blazor Applications (a subset at least) to be able to be compiled ahead of time.\\n\\nAoT opens the door to new scenarios, such as:\\n- Running on devices with heavy constraints (e.g. IoT)\\n- Running on devices with constrained sandboxes (e.g. iOS). While .NET runs in these devices today, Native AOT is a guarantee that we can run anywhere.\\n- Providing Web Based UIs for CLI tools (e.g. dotnet tools).\\n\\nIt also enhances Blazor\\u0026#39;s ability to run on existing scenarios:\\n* Serverless (e.g. Azure Functions)\\n* Containers (e.g. Kubernetes)\\n\\nIn general, AoT brings in the following benefits:\\n* Reduced app size\\n  * This is important for cloud scenarios where its desirable to achieve higher container density.\\n* Faster startup:\\n  * This impacts cold starts of the application, which is important in serverless contexts.\\n  * Scale out of rolling updates in Cloud scenarios.\\n* Reduced memory demand:\\n  * AoT apps generally run with less memory compared to JIT apps, since there are many runtime components that are not needed.\\n* Increased performance:\\n  * Many of the constraints imposed by AoT are addressed via optimizations that can be applied at compile time, which in many cases\\n    leads to better performance.\\n* Enhanced security:\\n  * AoT apps are less susceptible to runtime attacks, since the code is already compiled and there is no JITing happening at runtime.\\n  * When running in container scenarios, you can \\u0026#34;chisel\\u0026#34; the container to only have the minimum code needed for the app to run, reducing the surface attack area.\\n\\n## Goals/Scope of the work\\n* Investigate and list all the blockers that prevent the app from being AoT.\\n* Understand the available solutions for each problem (source generation, etc.)\\n* Identify the fixes that we think are valuable for other reasons (perf, better trimming, etc.)\\n* Prioritize the set of changes we want to tackle in .NET 9.0 to drive towards this scenario (low hanging fruit, performance, trimming)\\n\\n## Reasoning\\n\\nWe only get the benefits of AoT if we remove all the blockers, so we want to reduce the cost as much as possible by making changes that provide immediate value for other reasons (perf, trimming, etc).\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/51598\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"Priority:1\",\"NativeAOT\",\"triaged\",\"Pillar: Technical Debt\"],\"assignees\":[\"javiercn\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":18,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":48,\"+1\":31,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":5,\"hooray\":3,\"rocket\":5,\"eyes\":4},\"created_at\":\"2023-10-24T11:04:05Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-04-03T18:51:44Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":true,\"sub_issues_summary\":{\"total\":2,\"completed\":0,\"percent_completed\":0},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-26T22:11:48.970Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 7092b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":58811,\"title\":\"[Blazor] Improving ASP.NET Core integration\",\"body\":\"There are certain design choices in components that Blazor ships out of the box that make it hard to write applications that can work seamlessly on SSR scenarios and on interactive modes. This causes friction as there are many cases where the behavior is different on SSR and on Interactive sessions and developers have to account for both cases. Below is a non-exhaustive list of improvements that we can do to improve some of these experiences:\\n* Routing:\\n  * There are two routers, one on the server (ASP.NET Core) and one on the client. We\\u0026#39;ve merged the two implementations for the most part, but there are details that still cause confusion.\\n   * The need to declare additional assemblies in two locations: We should make the endpoint in ASP.NET Core pass along the configured assemblies to the client project via persisted state or some other mechanism.\\n   * Differences in handling `NotFound`: On SSR scenarios this is represented by an endpoint, on the interactive router with a `RenderFragment`. We should extend the router to take in a `NotFoundPage` parameter that can be used during SSR and Interactive rendering to display not found content.\\n   * Lack of `NavigationManager.NotFound()` or equivalent API for triggering `NotFound` on Blazor applications. This would trigger a 404 response on SSR scenarios that would render the `NotFound` page/component and on InteractiveScenarios it would signal any registered callback (the router) the equivalent situation (which would trigger the render).\\n   * Similar deal for triggering errors through an `Error` page.\\n * Authentication:\\n   * In ASP.NET Core you can use `Challenge` to trigger/start the authentication process. There is no Blazor equivalent for it, so users end up having to manually redirect users on interactive sessions.\\n   * We should extend `AuthenticationStateProvider` or similar APIs to support this type of scenario. On interactive sessions, a `Challenge` for a scheme will always result in a redirect (maybe challenge is not the right way to call this, and we should be using `RedirectToLogin` or some other verb. For server scenarios the information about the configured schemes is already available. For `WebAssembly` scenarios, information about the redirect URL can be provided via some mechanism like PersistedState. For schemes that need to generate additional information (like nonces, etc.) they\\u0026#39;ll be extended to add at least a new endpoint (maybe two) to handle the bootstrapping of the authentication process so that interactive clients (like webassembly) can redirect to a well-known URL to start the process.\\n* Lazy loading:\\n  * With prerendering, it can happen that we prerender a path that requires lazy loaded assemblies to render. The current APIs don\\u0026#39;t offer a way to make sure those assemblies are loaded before the page tries to render, which results in failures when the app goes interactive. We need:\\n  * A `LazyAssemblyLoader` implementation for prerendering (if you try to do this on any current .NET version it will fail).\\n  * For a given page, a list of all the dependent assemblies that are lazy loaded.\\n    * The ability to determine if they need to be immediately loaded for the page to render (for example, if the page references a type `B` that lives on a lazy loaded assembly on its `type definition` (`class A { public B BProp { get; set; } })` or if it can be delayed (because B is only used inside a method body).\\n  * A way to tell the runtime to load those assemblies when booting webassembly as we know they\\u0026#39;ll be needed immediately.\\n* Built-in components:\\n  * In general, we need to look at every component that we ship and ensure there\\u0026#39;s a way for them to work on each render mode in a reasonable way across render modes.\\n  * QuickGrid.\\n  * NavLink.\\n  * EditForm.\\n  * Section(s)\\n  * Cascading parameters.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/58811\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Pillar: Dev Experience\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":5,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":5},\"created_at\":\"2024-11-06T09:38:38Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-26T13:05:35Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":true,\"sub_issues_summary\":{\"total\":7,\"completed\":4,\"percent_completed\":57},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-26T22:11:50.017Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5692b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":63127,\"title\":\"Expose BearerTokenHandler from Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication\",\"body\":\"\\n\\n## Summary\\n\\nMake [BearerTokenHandler](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Security/Authentication/BearerToken/src/BearerTokenHandler.cs) public (instead of internal sealed) to allow customization by overriding its behavior, particularly HandleSignInAsync.\\n\\nThe alternative is creating my own handler which inherits from [SignInAuthenticationHandler](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Security/Authentication/Core/src/SignInAuthenticationHandler.cs#L14) and implement token authorization myself. This has the possible benefit of allowing custom BearerTokenOptions but is otherwise mostly identical to the existing BearerTokenHandler.\\n\\n## Motivation and goals\\n\\nI am trying to use AspNetCore.Authentication in combination with ASP.NET Core Identity taking advantage of user and role management. However, in order to comply with company wide API specifications I want to customize the sign in token response.\\n\\nMy goal is to use given access and refresh tokens with all the claims that Asp automatically includes but customize the response body of my sign in endpoint. In other word serving the pregenerated tokens in a different package.\\n\\n## In scope\\n\\n- Add custom fields to response body on HandleSignInAsync\\n- Services.AddBearerToken() using custom Handler\\n\\n## Out of scope\\n\\n- Custom BearerTokenOptions\\n- Updating AspNetCore.Idenity.AddIdentityApiEndpoints\\n\\n## Risks / unknowns\\n\\n- Other devs might overcomplicate things by overriting the BearerTokenHandler instead of using existing configuration capabilities\\n- Overwriting a crucial security class might encompass security risks by introduced by the developer. However, the other classes in Authentication are public as well.\\n- Other authentication handlers in ASP.NET Core (like JwtBearerHandler, CookieAuthenticationHandler, etc.) are public and overridable. This consistency would support advanced customization scenarios while maintaining the intended structure of the authentication system.\\n\\n## Examples\\n\\n```\\n// ApplicationBearerTokenHandler.cs\\npublic class ApplicationBearerTokenHandler(\\n    IOptionsMonitor optionsMonitor,\\n    ILoggerFactory loggerFactory, UrlEncoder urlEncoder\\n    ) : BearerTokenHandler (optionsMonitor, loggerFactory, urlEncoder)\\n{\\n...\\n}\\n\\n// Program.cs\\nbuilder.Services.AddAuthentication(IdentityConstants.BearerScheme)\\n    .AddBearerToken(IdentityConstants.BearerScheme);\\n\\n```\\n\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/63127\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"CGessinger\",\"id\":52929647,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/CGessinger\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52929647?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-auth\",\"design-proposal\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":2,\"+1\":2,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-08-05T09:31:44Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-11T17:31:11Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

It is clear that this is a confusing aspect for customers and that they run into issues when they inadvertently introduce problematic patterns in their apps, like components rendering a large set of elements which can cause the memory to grow significantly.\\n\\nWhen a customer finds itself in this situation, they generally open an issue with us that suggest there is a memory leak in the framework (which has not been the case so far) and we get into a discussion where we explain how Blazor deals with circuits, how memory works in Server GC and how to troubleshoot memory issues. The general points that people miss are:\\n* Circuits are alive for a given time after the session ends (up to a maximum number of circuits) to support reconnection.\\n* The server will only collect the circuits when it triggers a collection for the generation they live in, and in general, they will tend to go to Gen2.\\n* Server GC will only trigger a Gen2 collection when the server is running low on memory.\\n\\nIt will be extremely helpful if we can add additional diagnostics to help bring visibility into some of the internal aspects of how Blazor server operates. Specifically:\\n* dotnet-counters to track on a given server instance over time:\\n  * The number of connected circuits.\\n  * The number of disconnected circuits.\\n\\nThis makes it trivial to prove that we are handling the circuit lifetime correctly (or to spot when we are not) and since all the allocated framework memory is rooted by a circuit, it makes it easy to prove that the memory issue is not on the framework.\\n\\nFurther diagnostics to help identify problematic circuit instances using clrMD to identify circuits consuming a large amount of memory. We can do this as follows:\\n* Attach to the live process (or a memory dump).\\n* Walk the heap to find all the CircuitHost instances.\\n* For each CircuitHost instance, introspect its renderer and look at the ComponentState instances.\\n* For each ComponentState, we look at the backing field for the CurrentRenderTree\\n* On the RenderTreeBuilder we look at RenderTreeFrameArrayBuilder we look at the _items field to check the length of the array as well as the `_itemsInUse`.\\n* With this information, we can point out when a component rendered a large number of elements in the past or is currently rendering a large number of elements.\\n  * If it is currently rendering a large number of elements, `_itemsInUse` will be large.\\n  * If it has rendered a large number of elements in the past `_items` will be large.\\n\\nWith this data, we should be able to point out what components rendered a large number of elements currently or in the past as well as what circuit they belong(ed) to and its current state (whether the circuit is active, disconnected, or waiting to be collected) and it should also help discard the framework or the component rendering as the source of the memory issues.\\n\\nNote that this could also be extended to use something similar to `!objsize` on a component instance to track how much memory that component is allocating, which in turn would help identify components in the app that are holding on to a lot of memory (think for example a component that has a large list in memory).\\n\\nThis last bit is not only useful for Blazor Server but it might be useful too for Blazor Webassembly and Desktop.\\n\\nAnother way to identify issues with the app this issue would be to check the `ArrayPool` to identify large buffers that might have been allocated by the app in the past.\\n\\nExamples of issues in this area in the past (there are likely more):\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43221\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/39238\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/39156\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33547\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33077\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/32588\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30210\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/21991\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/18556\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17945\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/14545\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/10623\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43513\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-server\",\"Pillar: [2026-08-26T22:11:53.821Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5870b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":68801,\"title\":\"Remove the Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults OTLP export workaround after OpenTelemetry supports async export\",\"body\":\"### Description\\n\\nThe Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults template currently uses `BackgroundExportHandler` to work around synchronous OTLP export on single-threaded WebAssembly.\\n\\nOpenTelemetry\\u0026#39;s OTLP exporter calls:\\n\\n```csharp\\nHttpClient.SendAsync(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult()\\n```\\n\\nThis can stall when the HTTP pipeline performs asynchronous work. The template handler avoids that stall by capturing the request, immediately returning a synthetic successful response, and sending the real request asynchronously through a Polly resilience pipeline.\\n\\nOpenTelemetry added task-based batch and metric workers for single-threaded WebAssembly in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#6379, but the worker still invokes the synchronous exporter contract. The remaining limitation is tracked by open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708.\\n\\nOnce that issue is resolved and the fix is available in a stable OpenTelemetry release, remove the template workaround and use the standard OTLP exporter implementation.\\n\\n### Proposed changes\\n\\n- Update the Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults OpenTelemetry dependencies to a stable version containing the fix for open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708.\\n- Delete `BackgroundExportHandler.cs`.\\n- Remove the custom `IPostConfigureOptions` configuration that supplies `BackgroundExportHandler`.\\n- Remove the custom `ResiliencePipelineBuilder` configuration.\\n- Remove the `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` dependency if it is no longer otherwise needed.\\n- Configure logs, traces, and metrics using the standard `AddOtlpExporter` APIs.\\n- Allow OTLP exporters to use the normal HTTP client integration without bypassing globally configured asynchronous handlers such as service discovery.\\n\\n### Validation\\n\\nAdd or update browser integration coverage to verify that, in single-threaded Blazor WebAssembly:\\n\\n- Logs, traces, and metrics are exported successfully over OTLP/HTTP.\\n- Export works when `IHttpClientFactory` includes an asynchronous delegating handler, including the globally configured service-discovery handler used by the template.\\n- Export requests are not reported as successful before the HTTP operation completes.\\n- Export failures are surfaced through normal OpenTelemetry diagnostics.\\n- Retry, timeout, flush, and shutdown behavior use OpenTelemetry\\u0026#39;s standard semantics without fire-and-forget requests.\\n- No provider must be manually resolved to initialize OpenTelemetry; normal `IHostedService` startup remains sufficient.\\n\\n### Dependencies\\n\\nBlocked by:\\n\\n- open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708\\n\\nRelated:\\n\\n- #64574\\n- #64890\\n- #67259\\n- #67267\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68801\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-26T11:52:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T11:56:38Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The page renders its static markup, `blazor` initialises, and\\nthen the runtime dies at startup with:\\n\\n```\\nError: AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage (Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:\\nhttp://127.0.0.1:5300/_framework/resource-collection.ty4X_.js)\\nTypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../_framework/resource-collection.ty4X_.js\\n    at un (.../_framework/dotnet.runtime..js)\\n    at rn.resolve_or_reject (.../_framework/dotnet.runtime..js)\\n    ...\\n    at .../_framework/dotnet.native..wasm:wasm-function[298]\\n```\\n\\nNothing is rendered by any `InteractiveWebAssembly` component; the page sits on its static content.\\n\\n**It is load-dependent, not random.** With one browser at a time it does not occur at all. With eight\\nconcurrent browsers it affects roughly half of page loads.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe runtime starts on every load. Concurrency between independent browser instances should not affect\\nwhether an app boots.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n**Repro: https://github.com/Memphizzz/BlazorBootBugRepro**\\n\\n```bash\\ngit clone https://github.com/Memphizzz/BlazorBootBugRepro\\ncd BlazorBootBugRepro \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; ./repro.sh\\n```\\n\\nStock template, stock Chrome, no test framework and no third-party packages. The **only** addition to\\nthe template is a component rendered with `prerender: false`, so the marker it renders can come from\\nnowhere but a started runtime. The repo is the output of:\\n\\n```bash\\ndotnet new blazor -o BootRepro --interactivity WebAssembly --empty\\n```\\n\\n`BootRepro.Client/Booted.razor`:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\u003cp\\u003eWASM-BOOTED\\u003c/p\\u003e\\n```\\n\\nappended to `BootRepro/Components/Pages/Home.razor`:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\n```\\n\\nThen run N headless Chrome instances at the same URL, each with a fresh profile, and count the DOMs\\nthat do not contain the marker:\\n\\n```bash\\nfor i in $(seq 1 8); do\\n  google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-first-run \\\\\\n    --user-data-dir=\\u0026#34;$(mktemp -d)\\u0026#34; --virtual-time-budget=20000 \\\\\\n    --dump-dom \\u0026#34;http://127.0.0.1:5299/\\u0026#34; \\u0026gt; out-$i.html 2\\u0026gt;/dev/null \\u0026amp;\\ndone\\nwait\\ngrep -L wasm-booted out-*.html      # every file listed never started the runtime\\n```\\n\\n**Measured on the stock template above** (.NET 10.0.111, Chrome 143, Ubuntu 26.04):\\n\\n| concurrency | page loads | never started the runtime |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| **1 at a time** | 8 | **0** |\\n| **8 at a time** | 48 | **25** |\\n\\nThe serial arm is the control: same app, same browser, same budget, same marker — only concurrency\\ndiffers, so this is not the dump being taken too early.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n```\\nTypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:\\n  /_framework/resource-collection..js\\n```\\nsurfaced as `AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage` from `dotnet.runtime..js`. It reaches\\n`console.error` only — it raises no `error` or `unhandledrejection` event, so a page-level error hook\\nsees nothing.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.111\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n**ASP.NET Core**: 10.0.11 · **Chrome**: 143.0.7499.109 · **OS**: Ubuntu 26.04 (x64), WSL2 ·\\nno IDE (CLI).\\n\\n**Additional evidence from a private harness, offered because it narrows the mechanism.** The same\\nfailure occurs there, and a Chrome net-log (`--log-net-log`) of a failing browser shows:\\n\\n- **No `URLRequest` is issued for that module on the failing load** — not an error, not a hang: no\\n  request. [2026-08-26T22:11:55.640Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 7722b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":67980,\"title\":\"Blazor Web: exception during WASM root component activation is silently discarded — InteractiveAuto page stays a dead prerender with no error and no Server fallback\",\"body\":\"### Is there an existing issue for this?\\n\\n- [x] I have searched the existing issues\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\n\\n`WebAssemblyRenderer.OnUpdateRootComponents` fire-and-forgets the root component activation tasks:\\n\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/release/10.0/src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly/src/Rendering/WebAssemblyRenderer.cs#L72-L84\\n\\n```csharp\\ncase RootComponentOperationType.Add:\\n    _ = webRootComponentManager.AddRootComponentAsync(...);\\ncase RootComponentOperationType.Update:\\n    _ = webRootComponentManager.UpdateRootComponentAsync(...);\\n```\\n\\nIf activation throws (component constructor, DI resolution, a type-initializer failure in a dependency that only fails under Mono WASM, …), the fault is completely swallowed:\\n\\n- nothing in the browser console (no unhandled rejection, no `Blazor` error),\\n- no `blazor-error-ui`,\\n- no `ILogger` output,\\n- and for `InteractiveAuto`, **no fallback to Server**, even though the Server registration of the same page works (prerendering proves it).\\n\\nThe user is left on a permanently dead prerender. Worse: once Auto has committed to WebAssembly (runtime cached), even a **full page reload** of the affected page re-attempts WASM activation and dies the same way — there is no user-side recovery short of clearing the cache.\\n\\n**Real-world impact:** we hit this in production when a `TypeInitializationException` was thrown while constructing a ctor-injected DI service during activation of an `InteractiveAuto` page — but any exception thrown during activation triggers it; the specific trigger is irrelevant. Because the fault is discarded, diagnosing the underlying application-side bug took a multi-day investigation across CI bisects and Playwright traces, and ultimately required attaching an `AppDomain.FirstChanceException` handler in the WASM client — that handler is the only place the exception is observable. With ordinary error surfacing, the root cause would have been visible in the first failing run\\u0026#39;s browser console.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nSome combination of:\\n\\n1. The activation fault is logged (console + `ILogger`) and surfaces `blazor-error-ui`, like unhandled exceptions elsewhere in Blazor.\\n2. For `InteractiveAuto`, a failed WebAssembly activation falls back to the Server render mode instead of leaving a dead prerender (the server was able to render the page seconds earlier).\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nMinimal repro (unmodified `dotnet new blazor -int Auto` template plus only the changes listed in its README): https://github.com/alexaka1/repro-dotnet--aspnetcore-wasm-silent-activation\\n\\nA service is registered working on the server and with a throwing factory in the WASM client:\\n\\n```csharp\\n// Client Program.cs — simulates a dependency that only fails on the WASM runtime\\nbuilder.Services.AddSingleton(_ =\\u0026gt;\\n    throw new InvalidOperationException(\\u0026#34;Simulated: service construction fails on the WebAssembly runtime.\\u0026#34;));\\n```\\n\\n1. `dotnet run`, open `/counter` — first interactive visit renders Interactive **Server**.\\n2. Navigate Home ↔ Counter until Counter reports **WebAssembly** (Auto committed to WASM).\\n3. Click the nav link to `/crash` (enhanced navigation), a page that injects the service.\\n4. Observe: page reports `RendererInfo: Static, IsInteractive: false` forever; button does nothing; browser console and server logs are clean. A `FirstChanceException` hook is the only evidence of the `InvalidOperationException`.\\n5. Full reload of `/crash`: same dead result (Auto stays on WASM once cached).\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nOnly observable via `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.FirstChanceException`:\\n`System.InvalidOperationException: Simulated: service construction fails on the WebAssembly runtime.`\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.302\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n- ASP.NET Core version: 10.0.10 (behavior also reproduced on 10.0.9).\\n- Existing-issue search: `AddRootComponentAsync`, `OnUpdateRootComponents`, \\u0026#34;auto mode fallback\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;interactive auto stuck static\\u0026#34; — closest is #64508 ([Blazor] Unify root components initialization paths), which covers the divergent init paths but not the swallowed activation fault or the missing fallback.\\n- The same silent-discard exists for the `Update` operation.\\n- Happy to contribute a fix if you can indicate the preferred direction (await + log + error UI, vs. propagating the fault to enable Auto fallback).\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67980\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"alexaka1\",\"id\":22166651,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/alexaka1\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/22166651?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-07-23T14:16:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T07:22:48Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

This would also require a configuration surface needs to be designed to allow it to be configured and have sensible built-in defaults for redaction.\\n\\nThe second could be argued to be optional if HTTP QUERY is fully supported (see #63276, #65489, #65714).\\n\\nThere was a similar discussion around that for HttpClient\\u0026#39;s instrumentation, and they decided to not implement it: The .NET/JS interop can continue using shared memory if we find it\\u0026#39;s necessary to have good perf on those older browsers (and thread safety is not difficult because it\\u0026#39;s all synchronous).\\n * **In a web worker (background thread) on more up-to-date browsers**. The .NET/JS interop will need to work by serializing any data that is being transferred rather than passing pointers [1].\\n\\nThis will be advantageous because then, even if your .NET code does something that locks up the CPU (such as a GC cycle), the UI will remain perfectly smooth (e.g., during animations or scrolling, or while the user is typing quickly into a textbox).\\n\\nThe existing UI update mechanism is designed around transferring batches of minimal diffs from .NET to JS, so it shouldn\\u0026#39;t be hugely difficult to have it express those diffs as serialized data rather than pointers into the WASM memory space. We\\u0026#39;ll have to be careful around things like event handling to ensure that the asynchrony can\\u0026#39;t result in inconsistency of behaviour versus the synchronous single-threaded model. For example, we will need to force all event delivery to be async as far as the JS side is concerned, even in the non-worker-thread case.\\n\\n*[1] Strictly speaking, we could also do it with shared memory on even newer browsers that support SharedArrayBuffer. But if we can get satisfactory perf without this, it would be better to serialize because it would mean fewer combinations of browser scenarios, and saves us having to deal with potentially complex thread-safety concerns on the .NET side.*\",\"state\":\"open\",\"state_reason\":\"reopened\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/5475\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"severity-minor\",\"affected-very-few\",\"not-on-roadmap\"],\"assignees\":[\"pavelsavara\"],\"milestone\":\".NET 12 Planning\",\"comments\":14,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":22,\"+1\":21,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":1,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2018-02-19T17:05:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T12:05:29Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":67768,\"title\":\"Run Blazor WebAssembly in a Web Worker\",\"state\":\"CLOSED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67768\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For example:\\n\\n * Render batches are communicated to JS via zero-copy shared memory rather than by serialization\\n * Events triggered from JS are always processed synchronously by .NET, so there\\u0026#39;s no need to queue them\\n\\nAt first glance, it appears to work with `true`, but that\\u0026#39;s a mirage: it does *not* guarantee correctness in that mode, because the core single-threadedness assumption is violated. For example, JS might raise event 2 before event 1 finished processing, and by the time event 1 is done, there might not even be an event 2 handler any more and then you have an error.\\n\\n### Why we\\u0026#39;re only just encountering this now\\n\\n1. We didn\\u0026#39;t have multithreading before\\n2. Even to the extent that we did have an early preview of multithreading, it worked by running .NET on the browser UI thread, so we could define that as the sync context and then all the same assumptions would remain valid within that sync context. But now .NET WebAssembly has just moved to the new \\u0026#34;deputy thread\\u0026#34; multithreading model (i.e., all .NET code is on a background worker), these assumptions are no longer valid (e.g., because the UI thread\\u0026#39;s JS can no longer communicate with .NET in a synchronous, blocking manner).\\n\\n### Ensuring correctness\\n\\nWe\\u0026#39;ve already solved all these problems in our other hosting environments, Server and WebView, because they\\u0026#39;ve always been innately asynchronous from the beginning. We would need to generalize/port all these mechanisms so they are shared with or copied by the WebAssembly renderer, JS interop, eventing system, etc.:\\n\\n- [ ] Change rendering to serialize renderbatches to JS instead of doing shared-memory reads\\n- [ ] Change the rendering flow so that the renderer\\u0026#39;s `UpdateDisplayAsync` returns a `Task` that doesn\\u0026#39;t complete until the JS side sends back an explicit acknowledgement of that renderbatch\\n- [ ] Review JS interop to make sure any low-level assumptions we\\u0026#39;ve made about synchrony during the internals of message passing are replaced by async assumptions\\n- [ ] Do the above without changing things for the **single-threaded** WebAssembly flavour, since (1) it would be breaking if for example synchronous UI updates became async, and (2) those perf optimizations are there for a reason, and we don\\u0026#39;t want to make rendering many times more expensive in cases where you\\u0026#39;d be serializing huge strings, for example. It\\u0026#39;s OK to have significant behavioral and performance changes when people opt into multithreading, but not when they don\\u0026#39;t.\\n\\n### Approach\\n\\nAs a broad strategy, I think we can:\\n\\n * Factor out some new `WebRenderer` subclass called something like `AsyncWebRenderer` that holds the common logic around serializing renderbatches and accepting the async renderbatch acknowledgements from JS. This can then be used by all of Server, WebView, and multithreaded-WebAssembly.\\n * Use our WebView implementation as the reference for how a complete, async-safe rendering and eventing model should work, because this was more recently implemented than Server and is generally simpler and cleaner. There\\u0026#39;s not a huge amount of code in it, really. If some extra work is needed to queue event notifications, for example, we should see that clearly from the WebView code.\\n\\nI suspect it\\u0026#39;s not necessary to have two different builds of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly`. The total amount of code that should differ between the threaded and not-threaded won\\u0026#39;t be very much. I expect we can just have two different `Renderer` subclasses and some if/else branches in the JS code.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54365\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"triaged\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-threading\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":26,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":47,\"+1\":30,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":17,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-03-05T10:02:51Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-04-21T00:06:24Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":true,\"has_children\":false,\"parent\":{\"number\":17730,\"title\":\"Real multithreading in Blazor WebAssembly\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17730\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

In Blazor we use the .NET trimmer to significantly reduce the publish size of Blazor WebAssembly apps. However, we don\\u0026#39;t currently use the .NET trimmer to its fullest potential. We currently configure the trimmer in a partial mode, which only trims assemblies that are explicitly marked as trimmable. This typically means that the app assembly itself and many dependencies are not trimmed. This is a conservative setting that optimizes for maintaining functionality over reducing app size. \\n\\nThe default trim mode for the .NET trimmer is to trim everything. This is the mode used by the .NET Native AOT workloads.Analyzers provide warnings if there are code paths in the app that are not safe to trim. Given how sensitive web apps are to download size and load time, it seems like doing full trimming should be the goal for Blazor.\\n\\nEnabling support for full trimming also is a potential solution to enabling a [single project model for Blazor Web Apps](#49079) that target both server and browser. When you multitarget a project, everything in the project is built for both targets unless you indicated otherwise. This is problematic for browser scenarios because you may potentially bring in dependencies, components, and code into the browser targeted build that are only needed on the server. However, if we could enable full trimming *and* indicate to the trimmer which components are setup to render on WebAssembly, then the browser build could be aggressively trimmed to remove any unwanted code and dependencies.\\n\\nEnabling support for full .NET trimming typically means removing any dynamic code path that are based on reflection. We would need to make Blazor apps trimmer friendly by removing this code using techniques like source generators. For example, in Blazor we use reflection as part of the component discovery process and in the render tree builder code generated by the Razor compiler. We\\u0026#39;re already working on enabling [component discovery through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48767). We also have on our backlog to [handle component parameters through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/29550). There may be other related work items as well.\\n\\nThere is also ecosystem impact of enabling full trimming by default. Many .NET libraries are not setup for trimming and would potentially need to be updated. It will take some time to work through these issues with the Blazor community. Certain features also simply wouldn\\u0026#39;t work with full trimming. For example, dynamically loading dependencies at runtime that are not known statically. For backwards compatibility, app developers can configure the trimmer to not trim assemblies that are not yet trimmer friendly. We\\u0026#39;d need to understand better all the cases that get impacted by full trimming and ensure we provide a reasonable user experience for addressing them.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/49409\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"Priority:1\",\"Pillar: Technical Debt\",\"feature-trimming\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":20,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":46,\"+1\":43,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":3},\"created_at\":\"2023-07-14T14:49:12Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-12-06T11:52:00Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

It is clear that this is a confusing aspect for customers and that they run into issues when they inadvertently introduce problematic patterns in their apps, like components rendering a large set of elements which can cause the memory to grow significantly.\\n\\nWhen a customer finds itself in this situation, they generally open an issue with us that suggest there is a memory leak in the framework (which has not been the case so far) and we get into a discussion where we explain how Blazor deals with circuits, how memory works in Server GC and how to troubleshoot memory issues. The general points that people miss are:\\n* Circuits are alive for a given time after the session ends (up to a maximum number of circuits) to support reconnection.\\n* The server will only collect the circuits when it triggers a collection for the generation they live in, and in general, they will tend to go to Gen2.\\n* Server GC will only trigger a Gen2 collection when the server is running low on memory.\\n\\nIt will be extremely helpful if we can add additional diagnostics to help bring visibility into some of the internal aspects of how Blazor server operates. Specifically:\\n* dotnet-counters to track on a given server instance over time:\\n  * The number of connected circuits.\\n  * The number of disconnected circuits.\\n\\nThis makes it trivial to prove that we are handling the circuit lifetime correctly (or to spot when we are not) and since all the allocated framework memory is rooted by a circuit, it makes it easy to prove that the memory issue is not on the framework.\\n\\nFurther diagnostics to help identify problematic circuit instances using clrMD to identify circuits consuming a large amount of memory. We can do this as follows:\\n* Attach to the live process (or a memory dump).\\n* Walk the heap to find all the CircuitHost instances.\\n* For each CircuitHost instance, introspect its renderer and look at the ComponentState instances.\\n* For each ComponentState, we look at the backing field for the CurrentRenderTree\\n* On the RenderTreeBuilder we look at RenderTreeFrameArrayBuilder we look at the _items field to check the length of the array as well as the `_itemsInUse`.\\n* With this information, we can point out when a component rendered a large number of elements in the past or is currently rendering a large number of elements.\\n  * If it is currently rendering a large number of elements, `_itemsInUse` will be large.\\n  * If it has rendered a large number of elements in the past `_items` will be large.\\n\\nWith this data, we should be able to point out what components rendered a large number of elements currently or in the past as well as what circuit they belong(ed) to and its current state (whether the circuit is active, disconnected, or waiting to be collected) and it should also help discard the framework or the component rendering as the source of the memory issues.\\n\\nNote that this could also be extended to use something similar to `!objsize` on a component instance to track how much memory that component is allocating, which in turn would help identify components in the app that are holding on to a lot of memory (think for example a component that has a large list in memory).\\n\\nThis last bit is not only useful for Blazor Server but it might be useful too for Blazor Webassembly and Desktop.\\n\\nAnother way to identify issues with the app this issue would be to check the `ArrayPool` to identify large buffers that might have been allocated by the app in the past.\\n\\nExamples of issues in this area in the past (there are likely more):\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43221\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/39238\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/39156\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33547\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33077\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/32588\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30210\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/21991\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/18556\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17945\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/14545\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/10623\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43513\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-server\",\"Pillar: It has a few pages rendered on the server (SSR) and a \\u0026#34;counter\\u0026#34; page configured as:\\n`@rendermode InteractiveAuto`\\nI don\\u0026#39;t know if it is important but server doesn\\u0026#39;t support web sockets - Blazor fallbacks to polling in server interactive mode.\\n\\nOld version worked correctly in Firefox with javascript.options.wasm disabled. WASM files were not loaded and the application was running in server interactive mode. Then I enabled the javascript.options.wasm  option and refreshed the page. The WASM files were loaded and the application worked in client interactive mode.\\n\\nCurrently (in .NET 8.0.2) \\u0026#34;counter\\u0026#34; page is prerendered on the server and displayed in the browser but browser displays this message in console:\\nUncaught (in promise) Error: This browser does not support WebAssembly.\\n\\nIn my opinion for pages (or whole application) configured to work as `InteractiveAuto` you should use server interactive mode if WASM is not available.\\n\\nYou can go even further. Let\\u0026#39;s assume my WASM application is published with support for SIMD instructions (this is default configuration in 8.0). Unfortunately they are not available in iOS 15.x. You should test for SIMD support and fallback to SSI mode in case it is not supported. Related issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48756\\n\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54233\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Andrzej-W\",\"id\":32604409,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Andrzej-W\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/32604409?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-02-26T20:52:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-02-18T15:25:30Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Create a new Blazor WebAssembly standalone app with the `blazor-wasm-servicedefaults` template\\n2. Wire it with an Aspire AppHost using `AddBlazorWasmProject` + `AddBlazorGateway` + `WithOtlpExporter`\\n3. Use .NET 11 preview 6 SDK (11.0.100-preview.6.26316.109)\\n4. Navigate to any page in the WASM app\\n5. Browser console shows: `AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage (CircularDependencyException, Microsoft.Extensions.Options.IOptionsFactory)`\\n\\n## Environment\\n\\n- .NET SDK: 11.0.100-preview.6.26316.109\\n- Aspire SDK: 13.4.5\\n- OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol: 1.15.3\\n- Browser: Chromium (Blazor WebAssembly)\\n\\n## Workaround\\n\\nUse `NullLoggerFactory.Instance` instead of resolving `ILoggerFactory` from DI:\\n\\n```csharp\\nbuilder.Services.AddSingleton\\u0026gt;(_ =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    var logger = Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions.NullLoggerFactory.Instance\\n        .CreateLogger(\\u0026#34;Aspire.OtlpExport\\u0026#34;);\\n    return new PostConfigureOptions(null, o =\\u0026gt;\\n    {\\n        o.HttpClientFactory = () =\\u0026gt; new HttpClient(new BackgroundExportHandler(pipeline, logger));\\n    });\\n});\\n```\\n\\nThis breaks the circular dependency at the cost of losing export failure logging.\\n\\n## Suggested Fix\\n\\nOptions to fix while preserving logging:\\n1. Use `NullLoggerFactory` as the default, then lazily swap in a real logger after the host is built\\n2. Accept an `ILogger` parameter in `BackgroundExportHandler` that lazily resolves from the service provider on first use\\n3. Register `BackgroundExportHandler` separately and inject a lazy `ILogger`\\n4. Move the `IPostConfigureOptions` registration to run after the OTel logging pipeline is fully wired (deferred configuration)\\n\\n## Affected Template\\n\\n`src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/content/BlazorWasmServiceDefaults-CSharp/Extensions.cs`\\n\\n(Also affects the playground sample at `playground/BlazorStandalone/BlazorStandalone.ClientServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs` in `dotnet/aspire`)\\n\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67259\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"bug\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-templates\"],\"assignees\":[\"javiercn\",\"Copilot\"],\"milestone\":\"11.0-preview7\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":1},\"created_at\":\"2026-06-17T11:37:23Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-27T13:38:46Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-07-27T13:38:46Z\",\"closed_by\":\"javiercn\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}
